results.title: Vanishing ideal of a point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a point $a \in \mathbb{C}^n$, the ideal of polynomials in $\mathbb{C}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ that vanish on $\{a\}$ equals the kernel of the evaluation homomorphism $\mathbb{C}[x_1, \ldots, x_n] \to \mathbb{C}$, $f \mapsto f(a)$.

results.title: Weak Nullstellensatz, kernel form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. An ideal $I$ of the polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ is maximal if and only if there is a point $a \in \mathbb{C}^n$ such that $I$ is the kernel of the evaluation homomorphism $\mathbb{C}[x_1, \ldots, x_n] \to \mathbb{C}$, $f \mapsto f(a)$.

results.title: Weak Nullstellensatz, quotient form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P_1, \ldots, P_m$ be polynomials in $\mathbb{C}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ and let $A = \mathbb{C}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(P_1, \ldots, P_m)$. An ideal $J$ of $A$ is maximal if and only if there is a common zero $a \in \mathbb{C}^n$ of $P_1, \ldots, P_m$ such that $J$ is the image in $A$ of the ideal of polynomials vanishing at $a$.

results.title: Projective indefinite orthogonal group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $p$ and $q$, let $J$ be the diagonal $(p+q) \times (p+q)$ real matrix whose first $p$ diagonal entries are $1$ and whose last $q$ are $-1$, and let $\mathrm{O}(p,q)$ be the group of real $(p+q) \times (p+q)$ matrices $A$ with $J A^{\mathsf{T}} J A = A J A^{\mathsf{T}} J = I$. The group $\mathrm{PO}(p,q)$ is the quotient of $\mathrm{O}(p,q)$ by its center.

results.title: Mostow rigidity, algebraic form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 3$, and let $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ be lattices in the projective orthogonal group $\mathrm{PO}(n,1)$: discrete subgroups that have a fundamental domain for their action by left multiplication and finite covolume with respect to Haar measure. Then every group isomorphism $f : \Gamma \to \Lambda$ is a conjugation: there is $g \in \mathrm{PO}(n,1)$ such that $f(\gamma) = g \gamma g^{-1}$ for all…

results.title: Smooth one-forms
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold (possibly with boundary or corners). A smooth one-form on $M$ is a smooth section of the cotangent bundle of $M$: a smooth choice of a linear map $\alpha_x : T_xM \to \mathbb{R}$ at each point $x \in M$.

results.title: Two-forms as fields of bilinear forms
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold (possibly with boundary or corners). A two-form on $M$ is here a smooth section of the bundle whose fiber at $x \in M$ is the space of bilinear maps $T_xM \times T_xM \to \mathbb{R}$; antisymmetry is not required.

results.title: Smooth vector fields
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold (possibly with boundary or corners). A smooth vector field on $M$ is a smooth section of the tangent bundle of $M$: a smooth choice of a tangent vector $X_x \in T_xM$ at each point $x \in M$.

results.title: Exterior derivative of a one-form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A two-form $d\alpha$ on $M$ is the exterior derivative of a one-form $\alpha$ on $M$ when, for all smooth vector fields $X, Y$ on $M$ and every point $x \in M$,

results.title: Contact condition for a one-form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a one-form and $d\alpha$ a two-form on $M$. The pair satisfies the contact condition when $d\alpha$ is the exterior derivative of $\alpha$ and, at every point $x \in M$, the covector $\alpha_x$ is nonzero and there are tangent vectors $u, v \in T_xM$ with $\alpha_x(u) = \alpha_x(v) = 0$ and $d\alpha_x(u, v) \ne 0$.

results.title: Reeb vector fields
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a one-form and $d\alpha$ a two-form on $M$. An assignment $R$ of a tangent vector $R(x) \in T_xM$ to each point $x \in M$ is a Reeb vector field for $(\alpha, d\alpha)$ when, at every point $x \in M$, $\alpha_x(R(x)) = 1$ and $d\alpha_x(R(x), v) = 0$ for all $v \in T_xM$.

results.title: Integral curves
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold (possibly with boundary or corners) and let $R$ assign to each point $x \in M$ a tangent vector $R(x) \in T_xM$. A curve $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to M$ is an integral curve of $R$ when $\gamma$ is smooth and $\gamma'(t) = R(\gamma(t))$ for every $t \in \mathbb{R}$.

results.title: Vector fields with a closed orbit
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold (possibly with boundary or corners) and let $R$ assign to each point $x \in M$ a tangent vector $R(x) \in T_xM$. We say that $R$ has a closed orbit when there are a curve $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to M$ and a real number $T > 0$ such that $\gamma$ is $T$-periodic, $\gamma$ is a smooth integral curve of $R$, and $\gamma$ is not constant.

results.title: Weinstein conjecture in dimension three (Taubes)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a nonempty compact Hausdorff smooth manifold without boundary, modelled on a real vector space of dimension $3$. Let $\alpha$ be a smooth one-form and $d\alpha$ a smooth two-form on $M$ satisfying the contact condition: $d\alpha$ is the exterior derivative of $\alpha$ and, at every point $x$, $\alpha_x \ne 0$ and $d\alpha_x(u, v) \ne 0$ for some $u, v \in \ker \alpha_x$. Let $R$ be a Reeb vector field…

results.title: Attractor of an iterated function system
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $(f_i)_{i < n}$ be a finite family of maps $X \to X$. A set $S \subseteq X$ is an attractor of the family if it is nonempty and compact and is fixed by the Hutchinson operator, that is, $S = \bigcup_{i < n} f_i(S)$.

results.title: Affine-symmetric iterated function system
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $(f_i)_{i < n}$ be a finite family of maps $f_i \colon \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^d$ on Euclidean space. The family is affine-symmetric with common contraction factor $\lambda$ if $0 < \lambda < 1$ and there are linear isometries $A_i \colon \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^d$ (orthogonal transformations) and vectors $\beta_i \in \mathbb{R}^d$ such that $f_i(x) = \lambda A_i(x) + \beta_i$ for every $i < n$ and…

results.title: Open set condition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite family of maps $f_i \colon \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^d$, $i < n$, satisfies the open set condition if there is a nonempty open set $G \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ such that $f_i(G) \subseteq G$ for every $i < n$ and the images $f_i(G)$ and $f_j(G)$ are disjoint whenever $i \neq j$.

results.title: Moran's equality for affine-symmetric iterated function systems
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $(f_i)_{i < n}$ be an affine-symmetric iterated function system on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with common contraction factor $\lambda \in (0,1)$ that satisfies the open set condition. Then every attractor $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ of the system has Hausdorff dimension

part.title: Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process
api: Pathwise solution of the Langevin equation

uses: Closure of Gaussian laws under L² limits

results.title: Covariance of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at zero
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The covariance function of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at `0`: `(σ² / (2θ)) (e^{-θ|t-s|} - e^{-θ(t+s)})` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 5.6). It is meant for `θ > 0` and times `s, t ≥ 0`; at `θ = 0` the division by zero makes it `0`.

results.title: Covariance of the stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The covariance function of the stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process: `(σ² / (2θ)) e^{-θ|t-s|}` (Uhlenbeck–Ornstein 1930). It is meant for `θ > 0`.

results.title: Symmetry of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck covariance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The OU covariance is symmetric.

results.title: Variance of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The variance of the OU process started at `0`: `(σ² / (2θ)) (1 - e^{-2θt})`.

results.title: Variance of the stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The stationary variance `σ² / (2θ)`.

results.title: Ornstein–Uhlenbeck covariance converges to the stationary one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Shifting both times by `h → ∞` turns `ouCovariance` into `ouStationaryCovariance`.

results.title: Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at zero
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: `X` is an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at `0` with rate `θ > 0` and noise amplitude `σ` under `P`: a centered Gaussian process with covariance `ouCovariance θ σ`. Only the finite-dimensional laws are fixed (no path regularity).

results.title: Stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: `X` is a stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process with rate `θ > 0` and noise amplitude `σ` under `P`: a centered Gaussian process with covariance `ouStationaryCovariance θ σ`. Only the finite-dimensional laws are fixed.

results.title: Doob's clock for the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process from zero
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Doob's clock `τ t = (e^{2θt} - 1)/(2θ)` for the process started at `0`. The value is nonnegative for every real `θ`, so `Real.toNNReal` only changes its type.

results.title: Doob's clock for the stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Doob's clock `t ↦ e^{2θt}/(2θ)` for the stationary process (positive for `θ > 0`).

results.title: Doob's time change of Brownian motion
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Doob's time change `t ↦ σ e^{-θt} B(τ t)` of a process `B`, with `τ = ouClock θ`.

results.title: Doob's stationary time change of Brownian motion
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Doob's stationary time change `t ↦ σ e^{-θt} B(e^{2θt}/(2θ))` of a process `B`.

results.title: Construction (Doob 1942)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The time change `σ e^{-θt} B((e^{2θt} - 1)/(2θ))` of a pre-Brownian motion is an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at `0`.

results.title: Construction (Doob 1942)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The time change `σ e^{-θt} B(e^{2θt}/(2θ))` of a pre-Brownian motion is a stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process.

results.title: Existence of a pre-Brownian motion on path space
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a probability measure on paths `ℝ≥0 → ℝ` under which the coordinate process is a pre-Brownian motion (Kolmogorov extension of the Brownian finite-dimensional laws).

results.title: Existence of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at `0` exists for every `θ > 0` and `σ`.

results.title: Existence of the stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process exists for every `θ > 0` and `σ`.

results.title: One-time law of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process from zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The one-time law of the OU process started at `0`: `X t ~ N(0, (σ² / (2θ)) (1 - e^{-2θt}))`.

results.title: The Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process from zero starts at zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The OU process of `IsOrnsteinUhlenbeckFromZero` starts at `0` almost surely.

results.title: Relaxation to stationarity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For the process started at `0`, `cov(X (s + h), X (t + h)) → (σ² / (2θ)) e^{-θ|t-s|}` as `h → ∞`.

results.title: Stationary law
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Each `X t` of a stationary OU process is `N(0, σ² / (2θ))`.

results.title: Gaussian process laws are determined by mean and covariance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The finite-dimensional laws of a real Gaussian process are determined by its mean and covariance functions: two Gaussian processes with the same means and covariances (possibly on different probability spaces) have the same finite-dimensional laws.

results.title: Time shifts of a stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A time shift of a stationary OU process is a stationary OU process.

results.title: Strict stationarity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every finite-dimensional law of a stationary OU process is invariant under time shifts.

results.title: Conditional expectation of a Gaussian process given its past
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a centered Gaussian process with `cov(X u, X t) = c cov(X u, X s)` for all `u ≤ s`, the conditional expectation of `X t` given the natural filtration at `s` is `c X s`.

results.title: Conditional law of a Gaussian process at one time given another
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a centered Gaussian process with `cov(X s, X t) = c Var(X s)`, the conditional law of `X t` given `X s = x` is `N(c x, Var(X t) - c² Var(X s))` for almost every `x`.

results.title: Mean reversion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For the OU process started at `0` and `s ≤ t`, `E[X t | F s] = e^{-θ(t-s)} X s`, where `F` is the natural filtration of `X`.

results.title: Mean reversion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For the stationary OU process and `s ≤ t`, `E[X t | F s] = e^{-θ(t-s)} X s`, where `F` is the natural filtration of `X`.

results.title: Transition law
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For the OU process started at `0` and `s ≤ t`, the conditional law of `X t` given `X s = x` is `N(e^{-θ(t-s)} x, (σ² / (2θ)) (1 - e^{-2θ(t-s)}))` for almost every `x`.

results.title: Transition law
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For the stationary OU process and `s ≤ t`, the conditional law of `X t` given `X s = x` is `N(e^{-θ(t-s)} x, (σ² / (2θ)) (1 - e^{-2θ(t-s)}))` for almost every `x`.

results.title: Pathwise solution of the Langevin equation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The explicit solution of the pathwise Langevin equation driven by a path `w`: `e^{-θt} x₀ + σ (w t - e^{-θt} w 0 - θ ∫_0^t e^{-θ(t-u)} w u du)`. This is `e^{-θt} x₀ + σ ∫_0^t e^{-θ(t-u)} dw(u)` after integration by parts (the Itô-integral form for a Brownian path is a wanted statement).

results.title: Continuity of the pathwise Langevin solution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The pathwise solution is continuous when the driving path is.

results.title: Pathwise Langevin equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a continuous path `w` and every real `t`, `ouPathSolution θ σ x₀ w` satisfies `x t = x₀ - θ ∫_0^t x + σ (w t - w 0)` (any real `θ`, `σ`, `x₀`).

results.title: Uniqueness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A continuous solution of `x t = x₀ - θ ∫_0^t x + σ (w t - w 0)` on `t ≥ 0` equals `ouPathSolution θ σ x₀ w` there.

results.title: Elementary Itô integrals agree for modifications
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Elementary Itô integrals against two modifications of the same process agree almost surely.

results.title: Adjoining an independent Gaussian variable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `X₀` is a real Gaussian random variable independent of the real Gaussian process `B`, the process indexed by `Option T` that is `X₀` at `none` and `B t` at `some t` is a Gaussian process.

results.title: Covariance of the Wiener integrals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Covariance of the Wiener integrals `I_t = ∫_0^t e^{θu} dB_u`: for a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` with increments independent of the past and `θ ≠ 0`, `E[I_s I_t] = (e^{2θ (s ∧ t)} - 1) / (2θ)`, by the martingale property and the Itô isometry.

results.title: The pathwise Langevin solution driven by Brownian motion is Gaussian
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a Brownian motion `B`, `θ ≠ 0`, any real `σ`, and a start `X₀ ~ N(0, v)` independent of `B`, the process `X t = ouPathSolution θ σ X₀ B t` (`t ≥ 0`) is a Gaussian process with `E[X t] = 0` and `cov[X s, X t] = e^{-θ(s+t)} (v + σ² (e^{2θ (s ∧ t)} - 1) / (2θ))` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 5.6).

results.title: The pathwise Langevin solution is an OU process
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Driven by a Brownian motion and started at `0`, `ouPathSolution` is an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at `0` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 5.6). No filtration and no measurability of the coordinates of `B` is assumed.

results.title: Stationary start
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Driven by a Brownian motion `B` and started from `X₀ ~ N(0, σ²/(2θ))` independent of `B`, `ouPathSolution` is a stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 5.6).

results.title: Restricted combinations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $Q$ of natural numbers and $n, k \ge 0$, the restricted combinations are the $k$-element subsets $s$ of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ such that $b - a \notin Q$ for all $a, b \in s$ with $a < b$. Since only distinct elements are compared, whether $0 \in Q$ makes no difference.

results.title: Number of restricted combinations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $Q$ of natural numbers and natural numbers $n$ and $k$, $S^Q_{n,k}$ is the number of $k$-subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ in which no two distinct elements differ by an element of $Q$.

results.title: Number of subsets avoiding a set of differences
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $Q$ of natural numbers and $n \ge 0$, $S^Q_n$ is the number of subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ in which no two distinct elements differ by an element of $Q$. That is, $S^Q_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} S^Q_{n,k}$, where $S^Q_{n,k}$ is the number of such subsets with $k$ elements.

results.title: Restricted combinations with no forbidden differences
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the number $S^{\emptyset}_{n,k}$ of $k$-subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ in which no two elements differ by an element of the empty set is the binomial coefficient $\binom{n}{k}$.

results.title: Subsets of $\{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ with no two consecutive elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are exactly $8$ subsets of $\{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ in which no two elements differ by $1$.

results.title: Forbidden differences m, 2m, …, jm and strongly restricted permutations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $m \ge 1$, $j \ge 1$, $n$ and $k$, the number of $k$-subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ in which no two elements differ by an element of $\{m, 2m, \dots, jm\}$ equals the number of permutations $\pi$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n + jm - 1\}$ such that $\pi(i) - i \in \{-m, 0, jm\}$ for every $i$ and $\pi$ has exactly $k$ excedances (points $i$ with $\pi(i) > i$).

results.title: The $(1,t)$-bonacci polynomials
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Fix a natural number $s$ and put $t = s + 1$. The $(1,t)$-bonacci polynomials $f^{(t)}_n(x)$, $n \ge 0$, are the polynomials with natural-number coefficients defined by $f^{(t)}_0(x) = 1$ and, for every $n \ge 0$, $f^{(t)}_{n+1}(x) = f^{(t)}_n(x) + x \, f^{(t)}_{n-s}(x)$ if $s \le n$ and $f^{(t)}_{n+1}(x) = f^{(t)}_n(x)$ if $n < s$.

results.title: Initial value of the $(1,t)$-bonacci polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $s$, the $(1,s+1)$-bonacci polynomial of index $0$ is $f^{(s+1)}_0(x) = 1$.

results.title: Recurrence for the $(1,t)$-bonacci polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $s$ and $n$ with $s \le n$, the $(1,s+1)$-bonacci polynomials $f^{(s+1)}_m(x)$, $m \ge 0$, satisfy $f^{(s+1)}_{n+1}(x) = f^{(s+1)}_n(x) + x \, f^{(s+1)}_{n-s}(x)$.

results.title: The $(1,t)$-bonacci polynomials below the recurrence range
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $s$ and $n$ with $n < s$, the $(1,s+1)$-bonacci polynomials $f^{(s+1)}_m(x)$, $m \ge 0$, satisfy $f^{(s+1)}_{n+1}(x) = f^{(s+1)}_n(x)$.

results.title: Counting strongly restricted permutations with displacements $-m$, $0$, $jm$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m, j, i, r$ be natural numbers with $j \ge 1$ and $r < m$, and let $F_j$ be the Fibonacci $j$-numbers: $F_j(0) = 0$, $F_j(n) = 1$ for $1 \le n \le j$, and $F_j(n) = F_j(n-1) + F_j(n-j-1)$ for $n > j$. Then the number of permutations $\pi$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, im + r - 1\}$ such that $\pi(x) - x \in \{-m, 0, jm\}$ for every $x$ equals $F_j(i+1)^{m-r} \, F_j(i+2)^r$.

results.title: Combinations avoiding an interval of differences with one value removed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$, $q$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $p < q < 2p$, let $Q = \{1, \dots, q\} \setminus \{p\}$, and let $S^Q_n$ be the number of subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ in which no two elements differ by an element of $Q$. Then $S^Q_n$ is the number of compositions of $n + q$ in which every part is either $1$ or of the form $q + 1 + jp$ for some integer $j \ge 0$.

results.title: Well-based sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite set $Q$ of natural numbers is well based (Kitaev; Valyuzhenich) if for every $x \in Q$ and every natural number $a$ with $0 < a < x$, at least one of $a$ and $x - a$ lies in $Q$.

results.title: Shift set of a binary subword
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $\omega$ and $l$, the shift set of $\omega$ with length $l$ is the set of $j \in \{1, \dots, l - 1\}$ with $\lfloor \omega / 2^j \rfloor \ne \omega \bmod 2^{l-j}$. When $\omega < 2^l$ is read as a binary word of length $l$, this says that the leftmost $l - j$ bits of $\omega$ differ from its rightmost $l - j$ bits.

results.title: Shift set of the subword 1010
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The shift set of the binary subword $1010$ of length $4$ (the number $10$) is $\{1, 3\}$.

results.title: Subword shift sets are well based
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $l$ be a natural number and $\omega$ a binary word of length $l$, read as a natural number $\omega < 2^l$. Then the set $Q$ of those $j \in \{1, \dots, l-1\}$ for which the leftmost $l - j$ bits of $\omega$ differ from its rightmost $l - j$ bits, that is $\lfloor \omega / 2^j \rfloor \ne \omega \bmod 2^{l-j}$, is well based.

results.summary: Let $V$ be a polynomial-time Turing machine that computes a Boolean function on pairs of bit strings, reading a pair $(a, y)$ as the bits of $a$, a separator, then the bits of $y$, and writing its answer as one bit. For every polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients, the reduction built from $V$ and $p$ is polynomial-time computable with respect to the canonical bit-string encodings.

results.title: Every NP problem reduces to dense CNF-SAT
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every decision problem $L$ in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to dense CNF-SAT: a polynomial-time computable map $f$ on bit strings such that, for every bit string $x$, $L$ accepts $x$ exactly when dense CNF-SAT accepts $f(x)$.

results.title: Cook-Levin for dense CNF-SAT
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Dense CNF-SAT is NP-complete: it lies in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to dense CNF-SAT.

results.title: DENTIST-S statistic
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The DENTIST-S statistic `(z_i - r z_c) ^ 2 / (1 - r ^ 2)` of a variant with `z`-score `zi`, given the `z`-score `zc` of the lead (putative causal) variant and the reference correlation `r` between them (Kanai et al. 2022, Equation 1). Meaningful for `r ^ 2 < 1`; for `r ^ 2 = 1` it is `0` by the convention `x / 0 = 0`.

results.title: Mean of the standardized DENTIST difference
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mean `(ρ - r) λ / √(1 - r²)` of the standardized DENTIST difference when the true correlation is `ρ`, the reference correlation is `r` and the lead variant has mean `λ`.

results.title: Variance of the standardized DENTIST difference
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The variance `(1 - 2 r ρ + r²) / (1 - r²)` of the standardized DENTIST difference when the true correlation is `ρ` and the reference correlation is `r`.

results.title: Exact law of the standardized DENTIST difference
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let `(z_i, z_c)` be jointly Gaussian with unit variances, correlation `ρ` (the covariance, as the variances are `1`), and means `ρ λ` and `λ`. For a reference correlation `r` with `r ^ 2 < 1`, the standardized difference `(z_i - r z_c) / √(1 - r²)` is Gaussian with mean `dentistMean ρ r λ` and variance `dentistVariance ρ r`.

results.title: DENTIST-S is chi-squared with one degree of freedom under correct LD
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: When the reference correlation equals the true correlation `ρ` (`ρ ^ 2 < 1`), the DENTIST-S statistic has the law of the square of a standard normal variable.

results.title: DENTIST-S is exactly `χ²₁` when the reference LD is right
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under the model of `map_standardized_eq_gaussianReal` with reference correlation equal to the true correlation `ρ` (`ρ ^ 2 < 1`), the DENTIST-S statistic has the `chiSquareMeasure 1` law, for every value `λ` of the lead variant's mean.

results.title: Unit-variance criterion for the DENTIST difference
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The standardized DENTIST difference has unit variance iff the reference correlation is `0` or equals the true correlation (for `r ^ 2 < 1`).

results.title: Zero-mean criterion for the DENTIST difference
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The standardized DENTIST difference has mean zero iff the reference correlation equals the true correlation or the lead variant has mean zero (for `r ^ 2 < 1`).

outside: The square of a standard normal variable is chi-square with one degree of freedom
